paper_metadata.title: Subtraction peri-ictal SPECT is predictive of extratemporal epilepsy surgery outcome

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used a consecutive sample of patients from a specialized center with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria and baseline characteristics. The participation rate was high (111 surgical patients, 36 included after specific exclusions), and the sample appears representative of the target population of intractable extratemporal epilepsy patients.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: 36 consecutive patients who had peri-ictal and interictal SPECT studies and extratemporal resective epilepsy surgery performed at Mayo Clinic Rochester between June 1993 and June 1997.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as patients undergoing evaluation for intractable partial epilepsy at a major tertiary center.

items.evidence_snippet: During the study period, 257 patients had ictal SPECT studies performed as part of the evaluation for intractable partial epilepsy. Of these patients, 111 subsequently had epilepsy surgery
items.reasoning: The recruitment flow from the total pool of SPECT patients to the surgical cohort is transparently reported.

items.evidence_snippet: Of the extratemporal lobe group, five were excluded from the study because they did not have interictal SPECT performed, and five others were excluded because they did not have at least 12 months of postoperative follow-up.
items.reasoning: Exclusion criteria are specific and related to the technical requirements of the prognostic factor (SISCOM) and the outcome (follow-up duration).

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.
risk_of_bias_assessment.evidence_snippet: All patients had at least 12 months of postoperative follow-up.
risk_of_bias_assessment.reasoning: The exclusion of 5 patients for follow-up is a small proportion of the surgical cohort, and the remaining 36 provide a robust sample for this type of surgical study.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (SISCOM) is defined with high technical detail. Measurement was performed by blinded reviewers, and the methodology for coregistration and thresholding was standardized and previously validated.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Hyperperfusion SISCOM images were created as described previously... thresholded to one SD level and hypoperfusion images were thresholded to both one and two SD levels.
items.reasoning: The technical parameters of the SPECT subtraction and MRI coregistration are well-defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: SISCOM images were independently reviewed for regional cortical localization by two primary reviewers (B.P.M., E.L.S.) who were blinded to the clinical data, results of other tests, and surgical outcome.
items.reasoning: Blinding and the use of multiple reviewers with a tie-breaker ensure reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Hyperperfusion images were thresholded to one SD level and hypoperfusion images were thresholded to both one and two SD levels.
items.reasoning: Standard deviation thresholds are used, which are standard in this field and not post-hoc optimized for this specific dataset.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The SPECT images were acquired with the same scanner within 2 to 3 hours after the injection of radioisotope, using an identical protocol for both peri-ictal and interictal studies.
items.reasoning: Protocols were standardized across the cohort.

items.reasoning: All included patients had the necessary scans for SISCOM analysis.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.
risk_of_bias_assessment.evidence_snippet: SISCOM images were independently reviewed... blinded to the clinical data, results of other tests, and surgical outcome.
risk_of_bias_assessment.reasoning: The combination of technical standardization and blinded clinical review minimizes measurement bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure control) was measured using a validated 12-point scale. While the reviewers of the outcome were not explicitly stated to be blinded to the SPECT results, the outcome itself is relatively objective (seizure frequency) and the follow-up duration was sufficient.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Outcome classification was based on the patients' state of seizure control at latest follow-up... classified according to a 12-point seizure frequency score
items.reasoning: The 12-point scale (modified Engel) is a standard and well-defined metric in epilepsy surgery.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Postsurgical outcome with respect to seizures was determined by review of the patients' medical records.
items.reasoning: Standardized medical record review was used for all participants.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.
risk_of_bias_assessment.evidence_snippet: Outcome classification was based on the patients' state of seizure control at latest follow-up.
risk_of_bias_assessment.reasoning: The use of a validated scale and a minimum 1-year follow-up provides a reliable outcome measure.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for major confounders like MRI and EEG findings using multivariable logistic regression. However, other potential confounders such as duration of epilepsy, specific pathology (beyond lesional/non-lesional), and medication changes were not explicitly adjusted for in the models.
